question: How does vibrational coherence in the ground electronic state affect the absorption rate and yield of population inversion under ultrashort laser pulses?
answer: Vibrational coherence in the ground electronic state significantly enhances both the absorption rate and final population inversion yield when using ultrashort laser pulses.  Full population inversion can be achieved with significantly lower pulse areas compared to systems initially in a single eigenstate, by leveraging parallel transfer through vibrational coherence. While full optimization of the initial state may be challenging, even a small contribution from an excited vibrational level in the initial superposition can lead to substantial yield enhancements. This coherence effect vanishes with longer laser pulses that resolve individual state-to-state transitions, highlighting the importance of ultrashort pulses for exploiting vibrational coherence in enhancing electronic absorption.

The paper aims to develop an analytical model to better understand and predict the features of electronic absorption in molecules, particularly focusing on the role of initial vibrational coherence in enhancing absorption rates and yields when using ultrashort laser pulses. The work also contrasts this behavior with the use of long laser pulses, where such coherence is shown to have no effect. The theory is validated through numerical simulations of the first absorption band of Na₂.
